# Vendored Svelte source fixture

`remove_typescript_nodes.5.56.3.js` is vendored VERBATIM from the Svelte
compiler at the pinned oracle version:

- Upstream: `svelte@5.56.3`
- Path in package: `src/compiler/phases/1-parse/remove_typescript_nodes.js`
- License: MIT (see `LICENSE` in this directory; Copyright (c) 2016-2025 Svelte Contributors)

## Why it is here

The native-Svelte component-name scope-view projection (`verter_compiler`
`SvelteScopeProjection`) mirrors how Svelte classifies each TypeScript AST node
— erase / scope-inert / unwrap / keep — for the sources Svelte COMPILES, so that
the emitted component function `name` deconfliction reproduces Svelte's own
runtime-binding set on those compile rows. (A Svelte REJECT or CRASH emits no
component and no name, so name-parity is VACUOUS there — Verter's disposition is
then characterized separately; see the honest qualification below.) The in-crate
conformance matrix
(`crates/verter_compiler/src/svelte/runtime/component_scope_projection_conformance_tests.rs`)
has two halves:

1. A source-derived HANDLER rail: it parses Svelte's complete
   `remove_typescript_nodes` visitor handler inventory from THIS vendored source
   with OXC, asserts a bijection with the committed `HandlerCoverage` rows (each
   mapping a handler to ≥1 committed corpus axis), and fingerprints each handler
   body as a drift tripwire — so any Svelte-version drift or an unhandled node
   kind trips it.

2. An ORACLE-DERIVED name-parity matrix. The committed corpus
   (`name_parity_corpus.json`) is generated by
   `scripts/gen-svelte-name-parity-corpus.mjs`, which plants an identifier per
   construct, sets `name=<planted identifier>`, runs the PINNED Svelte compiler
   OFFLINE, and records SVELTE'S OWN outcome (the emitted component-function name,
   a reject code, or — for a construct Svelte CRASHES uncoded on, e.g. a lone class
   index signature — a `crash` outcome). The corpus is currently 80 rows (72
   compile / 7 reject / 1 crash). The emitted-name pins therefore come from Svelte itself, so
   a projection that drops a reserved name REDs against Svelte's own outcome
   instead of matching a hand-authored value (the prior hand-pinned three-set
   matrix was self-confirming — a buggy projection plus a matching wrong pin both
   passed).

Parity is qualified HONESTLY, not claimed for every TS node: a Svelte-COMPILE
row asserts exact name parity (Verter's derived name == Svelte's emitted name);
a Svelte-REJECT row (every `enum` including `declare enum`, a value `namespace`,
a ctor param-property, an `accessor` field, a decorator, an `export default`)
carries no Svelte name, so name-parity is VACUOUS and Verter's disposition is
characterized separately with an EXACT reserved-set observation (a defensive
erase, or a preserved known-gap) — never a Svelte-parity claim; a Svelte-CRASH
row (a lone class index signature, on which Svelte crashes uncoded) is VACUOUS the
same way (Verter defensively erases it, does not crash); the `<T>x` angle
assertion is a Verter fail-closed row (the shared tsx reparse rejects it).

The matrix consumes ONLY these vendored/committed fixtures on the default run
(no live Svelte oracle, per the Testing-Hermeticity rule); optional
`svelte-oracle`-gated rails compare the vendored source to the installed
`node_modules` copy and re-run the corpus generator's `--check` against the
pinned compiler when that copy is present.

## Updating

The authoritative oracle-version anchor is the Rust constant
`SVELTE_ORACLE_VERSION` in
`crates/verter_compiler/src/svelte/runtime/component_scope_facts.rs`, which the
conformance matrix ties to the `svelte` version pinned in `pnpm-lock.yaml`. When
svelte is re-pinned:

1. bump `SVELTE_ORACLE_VERSION` to the new version;
2. re-vendor this file from the new version and rename it to
   `remove_typescript_nodes.<version>.js` (and update the `include_str!` path in
   the conformance matrix so a stale name cannot be retained);
3. re-verify the projection classifies the (possibly new) handler inventory —
   the matrix's source-derived bijection and body fingerprints will fail until
   every handler is classified consistently with the new source;
4. regenerate the oracle-derived name-parity corpus against the new pinned
   compiler: `node scripts/gen-svelte-name-parity-corpus.mjs` (the committed
   `name_parity_corpus.json` carries the new `svelte_oracle_version` and Svelte's
   fresh emitted-name / reject-code / uncoded-crash pins; `--check` and the
   `svelte-oracle`-gated freshness rail assert it stays in sync).
